h1: The 8 Best All-in-One Printers for Home Use of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best all-in-one printers for home use, from budget Canon and HP inkjets to an ink-tank Brother and a feeder-equipped model.
mainKeyword: all in one printer for home use
summary: The Canon PIXMA TR8620a is the best all-in-one for homes that use most features, from fax to an automatic feeder. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the better pick for steady document work, with a feeder and duplex printing at a lower price. Basic households can stay with the Canon TS4320 or HP DeskJet 4355.
intro: A home all-in-one is a bundle of features, and most households use only half of them. Fax is the classic example: it comes standard on several models, yet a printer that never faxes is paying for hardware it will not touch. What people actually miss is a feeder for scanning forms or a duplex unit that halves the paper pile.

We ranked eight all-in-ones from their listings, looking at functions, feeder, duplex, display and ink approach. Start with the tasks you do every week, then choose the cheapest model that covers them. Prices appear as buckets, and ink programs are noted only as trials.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR8620a All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Nearly every all-in-one feature, in one home-friendly body.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TR8620a prints, copies, scans and faxes, and adds an automatic feeder, wireless setup, AirPrint and Android support, Alexa compatibility and photo printing. It sits in the $100 to $200 range.

It leads because no other pick lists as many features in a single home-sized body. A household that actually scans stacks, sends the occasional fax and prints photos gets real value from it. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e gives you a feeder and duplex for less, but it leaves out fax and some of the mobile options.

Buy it if you want one machine to cover nearly every job. Skip it if your printing is occasional and simple, because you would be paying for hardware you will rarely use.
products.idealFor: Households that use most all-in-one features.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: ADF and duplex for home-office work without the fax extras.
products.description:
The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e prints, scans and copies with an automatic feeder and duplex printing. It includes a three-month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable features, and it is aimed at home-office work. Expect to pay $50 to $100.

It ranks second only because it skips fax and the extra mobile conveniences the Canon offers. For anyone whose work is documents, that omission hardly matters, and the feeder-plus-duplex pairing makes it the strongest value for steady paperwork. It costs less than the Canon too.

Buy it if you handle forms, reports or school work every week. Keep in mind the ink trial lasts only three months, so factor ongoing ink into your budget before you commit.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The same feeder-and-duplex idea, listed at a higher price bucket.
products.description:
The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 lists the same feeder, duplex printing, AI-capable features and three-month Instant Ink trial as the 8125e. It is a wireless home-office all-in-one, but it sits in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Third place is entirely about price. Because the headline features match the 8125e, a higher price brings no clear benefit. If both are sold at the same price on the day you shop, either will do, and the choice becomes one of stock and shipping.

Buy whichever 8125 costs less. Skip this one when the 8125e is cheaper, since the listing does not show any extra advantage. Do not assume that the higher price means a better printer.
products.idealFor: Buyers who find this variant at a good price.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Duplex printing in a compact single-tray body.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TS4320 prints, scans and copies, with duplex printing in a compact single-tray body. A one-year limited warranty covers it, and setup is described as easy. Prices run $50 to $100.

It ranks fourth because it has no automatic document feeder, which the HP units above include. In exchange you get a smaller footprint and a lower bill, plus two-sided printing that saves paper. For a household that mostly prints single pages, the missing feeder is a minor cost.

Buy it for light home use where duplex matters. Skip it if you scan multi-page documents, because every sheet has to go on the glass by hand.
products.idealFor: Light home use with two-sided printing.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen makes daily use less fiddly.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TS6520 prints, scans and copies with duplex printing, and adds a 1.42 inch OLED display and an intuitive control panel. It has no feeder, and it costs $50 to $100.

It lands fifth because the screen is a comfort feature rather than a capability. The TS4320 delivers the same core functions with less to learn. What the TS6520 offers is control on the device itself, which saves you opening an app for a quick copy.

Buy it if app-only control annoys you and you like pressing a button to copy. Skip it if you want a feeder, since neither Canon in this pair has one. The extra screen is nice, but not essential.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer with ADF
products.verdict: A feeder and fax for households that scan multi-page papers.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TR4720 prints, scans, copies and faxes, and includes an automatic document feeder and mobile printing support. The compact home design is wireless, and it costs $50 to $100.

It ranks sixth because duplex is not listed, whereas the HP units pair a feeder with two-sided printing. It does win on size and gives you fax, which the HP printers lack. The fax feature is legacy, but some households still need it.

Buy it if you scan multi-page forms and want an inexpensive way to do it. Skip it if you need duplex, because two-sided jobs mean flipping pages manually.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Print, scan and copy with simple setup, nothing more.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 prints, scans and copies, with simple wireless setup, a compact budget design and a three-month Instant Ink trial. There is no feeder, and no duplex is listed. Prices run $50 to $100.

It ranks seventh since it offers fewer features than the Canon models above. What it does, it does plainly: set it up quickly, print what you need, and scan single sheets. The ink trial can lower the first few months of costs.

Buy it for occasional home printing such as recipes, labels or the odd form. Skip it if you need a feeder or duplex printing, because the HP 8125e or the Canon TS4320 deliver those for similar money.
products.skipIf: You need a feeder or duplex.

products.name: Brother INKvestment 4355 Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One Printer (MFC-J4355DW)
products.verdict: Ink-tank economics and a manual feed slot for specialty paper.
products.description:
The Brother MFC-J4355DW prints, scans and copies using an ink-tank system. It has a 1.8 inch color display, a manual feed slot for envelopes and cardstock, and a Refresh Subscription trial. It is the most expensive pick, at $200 to $500.

It ranks last because it costs far more than the rest and lists no feeder. Its niche is specialty paper: the manual slot handles envelopes and cardstock that cartridge inkjets often struggle with. For ordinary documents, cheaper machines do the same job.

Buy it if you regularly print envelopes, cards or thick stock. Skip it if you mostly print documents, since the price premium will not pay back and the Canon TR8620a offers more features for less.

whatMatters.detail: An automatic document feeder, or ADF, pulls pages through the scanner without lifting the lid each time. It matters for multi-page forms, contracts and school packets. Look for ADF in the title or spec table. The Canon TR8620a, TR4720 and both HP OfficeJet Pro models list one.

Duplex printing prints both sides of the page automatically, saving paper and time on longer documents. Without it you flip pages by hand. Check the listing for the word duplex. The HP 8125e and the Canon TS4320 and TS6520 list it, while the Canon TR4720 does not.

Ink programs such as Instant Ink send cartridges for a monthly fee. On the HP models here, the offer is a three-month trial, not a lasting discount. Plan ongoing ink costs beyond that. Read the terms in the listing, and compare what you would pay once the trial is over.

A built-in display lets you copy and scan without an app. The Canon TS6520 has a 1.42 inch OLED screen, and the Brother has a 1.8 inch color display. It matters for quick jobs and for family members who dislike apps. Look for display size in the specs.

A manual feed slot accepts envelopes and cardstock outside the main paper tray. It matters only if you print them regularly. The Brother MFC-J4355DW lists one. Look for manual feed in the specifications, and check which paper weights and envelope sizes the manual says it supports.

cards.text: You use fax, a feeder and photos. The Canon TR8620a pulls them together.

faq.a: Only if you scan multi-page documents. The Canon TR8620a and TR4720 and both HP OfficeJet Pro models have one. For single pages, a model without a feeder like the Canon TS4320 costs less.
Paying for fax and a feeder that never get used. The Canon TR8620a is wonderful for busy households, but a family that prints occasionally is better served by the TS4320 or DeskJet 4355.
The three-month trials on the HP 8125e and DeskJet 4355 only cover the start. Check what the subscription costs afterwards, and compare it with buying standard cartridges before you decide.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Use the maker's app to join your wifi, then install the driver on each computer. HP and Canon models like the DeskJet 4355 and TS6520 both describe simple wireless setup in the listing.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet nozzles healthy?
faq.a: Print something every week or two so the ink does not dry in the nozzles. Inkjets such as the Canon TS4320 clog if left idle for long periods.

faq.q: Can I print from my phone?
faq.a: The Canon TR8620a lists AirPrint and Android compatibility, and the TR4720 lists mobile printing support. Both let you print without a computer, once the printer is on your wifi.

finalTake: The Canon TR8620a suits households that scan, fax and print photos. Document-heavy homes should choose the HP 8125e, and light users can buy the Canon TS4320 for duplex or the DeskJet 4355 for basic needs. Pay for the Brother only if envelopes and cardstock are a regular job.
